cbrt.signature: Exactly one finite binary64 Number operand; the result is Number and is nullable exactly when the operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique Number signature. No implicit conversion, distinct INT64, NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC, Decimal or non-finite overload is admitted.
cbrt.typing: Return Number with the operand nullability. Type-check the sole operand without evaluating it; the finite Number domain admits positive, negative, zero, subnormal and largest finite magnitudes.
cbrt.value: Return the real cube root, including negative inputs. Either zero sign produces canonical positive zero. NULL produces NULL. There is no additional value-domain failure for an admitted finite Number; reject non-finite operands and preserve the existing arithmetic failure for an unexpected non-finite result.
cbrt.algorithm: Use the same pinned portable MoonBit core Double cbrt primitive in src/scalar_numeric_kernel on JS, WebAssembly and Native (source manifest sha256:254e734f8e44242b835b0a6c2505011b5eea6b9883dfa3db8c1b74e061757e0b), through the existing canonical scalar owner and finite-result validation. Do not substitute pow(x, 1/3), logarithmic reconstruction or a frontend/Host evaluator. The compatibility target is the GoogleSQL finite-FLOAT64 cube-root operation. Preserve every existing numeric accuracy and exception contract. Identical admitted inputs and selected semantic contracts preserve exact logical Number bits across targets; no live-BigQuery last-bit equivalence is claimed.
cbrt.evaluation: Demand the sole child exactly once and preserve its failure before strict NULL propagation. Preserve enclosing lazy demand, retained roots, logical operand/result and control charges, live-value and workspace limits, and cooperative cancellation. Reuse the common continuation and canonical unary scalar evaluator.
cbrt.identity: The closed source is {cbrt: expression} and the closed machine node is {op: cbrt, body: expression_node}. CBRT selects this same direct unary operation. Retain the node and sole child without folding or duplication, including constants; earlier pinned contract bodies retain their identities.
